core_obligations: In Sites, Lemma \refsites-lemma-bigger-site we have seen that the functor f^-1 : \Sh((\Sch/S)_fppf) \to \Sh((\Sch'/S)_fppf) is fully faithful (see discussion in Topologies, Section \reftopologies-section-change-alpha).
Suppose that X' \in \Ob(\textitSpaces'/S) such that there exists U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_fppf) and a map U \to X' in \Sh((\Sch'/S)_fppf) which is surjective as a map of sheaves.
Now let X', U \to X' and R \to U \times_X' U be as in the statement of the lemma.
proof_roadmap: 第 1 步：In Sites, Lemma \refsites-lemma-bigger-site we have seen that the functor f^-1 : \Sh((\Sch/S)_fppf) \to \Sh((\Sch'/S)_fppf) is fully faithful (see discussion in Topologies, Section \reftopologies-section-change-alpha).
第 2 步：Suppose that X' \in \Ob(\textitSpaces'/S) such that there exists U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_fppf) and a map U \to X' in \Sh((\Sch'/S)_fppf) which is surjective as a map of sheaves.
第 3 步：Now let X', U \to X' and R \to U \times_X' U be as in the statement of the lemma.
difficulty_reason: H2: Preserve the exact original change-of-big-site hypotheses and the essential-image condition requiring small-site witnesses for both U and the relation U×_{X′}U. Full faithfulness itself is the cited bigger-site lemma; the counted nonroutine work is the reverse essential-image construction. The author bounds selected quasi-compact pieces of an etale presentation by size(U), constructs a bounded fppf refinement, and repeats the control on the relation to produce a small-site etale presentation U′/R′. The explicit cardinal-growth example explains why a small U alone is insufficient: the relation may grow like kappa^kappa. This addresses the stated size obstruction, not merely the forward preservation of representability or a universe-closure convention. Original omitted details and counterexample footnote retained, no proof supplementation.

dedup.basis: Existing7267 says enlargement preserves representable schemes and algebraic spaces;6945 is the corresponding stack-property preservation. The cardinal relation obstruction and reverse criterion are not concluded by those forward-preservation statements.
